executive_summary:
Nigeria’s GDP expanded 4.43% in Q2 2026, with real estate and construction contributing to growth as the non-oil sector strengthened. The 4.43% growth rate represents a 54 basis-point acceleration from Q1 2026 and a 20 basis-point improvement over Q2 2025, signaling sustained momentum in the sector despite broader macroeconomic headwinds. Infrastructure development in the Lekki-Epe corridor—including the upcoming Green Line Metro, Lekki Deep Seaport, and Dangote Refinery—continues to act as a primary catalyst for land value appreciation and demand in adjacent residential sub-markets.

The MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF) has disbursed N140 billion in mortgage loans to 2,000 Nigerians across 27 states since April 2025, with Lagos and Abuja accounting for the largest share of applications. This expansion of formal mortgage financing directly addresses structural affordability constraints and increases the addressable buyer pool for mid-market residential products, particularly in Lagos and Abuja. The programme’s 99-year tenor and rates starting at 9.75% represent a material easing of long-term credit access compared to historical norms.

A new diaspora mortgage scheme launched by the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) enables eligible Nigerians abroad to access formal mortgage finance for residential properties in Nigeria, marking a significant expansion of the housing finance system. The scheme, officially launched in London on August 7, targets the >$90 billion in diaspora remittances recorded between 2020–2024, which grew 9% YoY in 2024, positioning diaspora buyers as a high-conversion segment for premium and mid-market residential products.

Global supply chain disruptions and heightened shipping costs from the Middle East conflict are intensifying construction cost inflation and project financing expenses in Nigeria’s real estate sector. The conflict has slowed market transactions, increased project financing expenses, and worsened Nigeria’s housing crisis, with the real estate and construction sector among the worst hit. This macroeconomic pressure risks compressing margins and delaying project timelines, particularly for developers reliant on imported construction inputs.

themes.label: MREIF Mortgage Disbursement Acceleration
themes.what_happened: MREIF disbursed N140 billion in mortgage loans to 2,000 Nigerians across 27 states since April 2025, with Lagos and Abuja representing the largest share of applications.
themes.why_it_matters_to_mixta: Directly expands the addressable mortgage-backed buyer pool for mid-market residential products in Lagos and Abuja, particularly for products positioned within the MREIF-eligible price band. The programme’s 99-year tenor and 9.75% rates improve affordability and long-term financing stability, reducing receivables risk and accelerating sales conversion.
themes.recommendation: Prioritize MREIF-compliant product positioning and pricing in Lagos and Abuja, and accelerate engagement with Access Bank to formalize mortgage partnerships for eligible products. Reallocate sales resources to target MREIF beneficiaries in the 2,000-loan cohort.

themes.label: Diaspora Mortgage Scheme Launch
themes.what_happened: FMBN launched a diaspora mortgage loan scheme enabling eligible Nigerians abroad to access formal mortgage finance for residential properties in Nigeria, with the product launched in London on August 7.
themes.why_it_matters_to_mixta: Opens a high-conversion channel for diaspora buyers, leveraging the >$90 billion in diaspora remittances (2020–2024) growing 9% YoY in 2024. Diaspora buyers are explicitly targeted in the 'Own It 4 Sure' positioning, and the scheme addresses one of the '7 fears' (FX volatility) by enabling FX-locked pricing.
themes.recommendation: Activate the diaspora sales channel (sales_diaspora@mixtafrica.com) immediately, and align product offerings with diaspora preferences (e.g., premium Lakowe Lakes products, USD-priced units). Develop targeted marketing collateral for the diaspora mortgage scheme and partner with FMBN to co-promote eligible products.

sourceArticles.title: Diaspora Mortgage Scheme Opens Fresh Opportunities for Nigeria’s Housing Market

themes.label: Construction Cost Inflation from Middle East Conflict
themes.what_happened: The Middle East conflict has increased shipping costs, supply chain disruptions, and project financing expenses in Nigeria’s real estate sector, slowing transactions and worsening the housing crisis.
themes.why_it_matters_to_mixta: Rising construction costs compress margins and risk schedule slippage on projects reliant on imported inputs (e.g., BAFF, drainage, roadworks). This pressure is particularly acute for affordable-to-mid-market products where price sensitivity is high, and could delay Phase 1 delivery of Garden City Golf Annexe in Port Harcourt.
themes.recommendation: Reassess procurement strategies for imported materials, secure forward contracts where possible, and accelerate cost pass-through negotiations with contractors. Prioritize local sourcing for high-volume inputs to mitigate FX risk.

themes.label: Lekki-Epe Corridor Infrastructure Catalyst
themes.what_happened: Nigeria’s GDP growth of 4.43% in Q2 2026 is supported by real estate and construction, with the Lekki-Epe corridor’s infrastructure (Green Line Metro, Lekki Deep Seaport, Dangote Refinery) acting as a primary growth driver.
themes.why_it_matters_to_mixta: The corridor’s infrastructure directly drives land value appreciation and demand in adjacent sub-markets (e.g., Lakowe, LNT), enhancing the premium positioning of Lakowe Lakes Golf Estate and LNT commercial plots. The Green Line Metro (68km, 177 stations) and Dangote Refinery (135,000+ jobs at maturity) are the next catalysts to track for completion/delay news.
themes.recommendation: Monitor Green Line Metro and Dangote Refinery progress for timing signals to adjust sales activation and pricing strategies in Lakowe and LNT. Prioritize infrastructure-led marketing narratives for premium products.
